items.body: This guide helps you create a port-forward rule in your router's browser-based admin page for Generic Router.

bullets: Confirm the host Mac is the device that will receive the forward.
Keep the router login open so you can return to the forwarding page if the firmware hides advanced settings.
Have the host Mac's local IP ready: 192.168.1.42.
Common admin addresses for this guide: 192.168.1.1, 192.168.0.1, 10.0.0.1.
Recommended protocol guidance: Forward TCP for the Java server on port 25565.
Bedrock port: 19132 (usually UDP, when Bedrock/Geyser is enabled)

items.title: Get the values you need first
items.body: Before changing the router, note the host Mac's local IP, the Java port, and the Bedrock port if Bedrock is enabled.

items.title: Log into the router
items.body: Open the router admin page in a browser. Common addresses include 192.168.1.1, 192.168.0.1, and 10.0.0.1. Exact screens vary by firmware.

items.title: Find the forwarding section
items.body: Look for Port Forwarding, NAT Forwarding, Virtual Server, Applications & Gaming, Firewall Rules, or Advanced NAT.

items.title: Create the rule
items.body: Target the host Mac's local IP. For Java, forward TCP on the configured Java port. If Bedrock is enabled, also forward UDP on the configured Bedrock port.

items.title: Save or apply the change
items.body: Save the new rule, apply changes, and reboot the router only if the firmware asks for it.

items.title: Test from outside your network
items.body: After the rule is saved, test from a different network. If it still fails, continue into troubleshooting instead of guessing.

items.title: Transparency
items.body: Exact labels and screens vary by firmware version and router vendor.

items.title: ISP vs router
items.body: Your internet provider name is not always the device you configure. You may have ISP hardware plus your own router.
If the rule still does not work after you save and test from another network, continue with the matching troubleshooting topics below instead of guessing.

notes: resolvedString(for: .bedrockPort) only checks whether bedrockPort is set, not bedrockEnabled -- with bedrockPort=19132 and bedrockEnabled=false, the bedrock_port placeholder still resolves to "19132" while bedrock_enabled resolves to "No". No unresolvedTokens.
